title: Repeater alphabet soup
idea: Most repeater terms are a key for getting in: the right offset, tone or code. On DMR, a talkgroup ID picks who you hear.

items: Can hear the repeater but can't get in
Check the offset, the CTCSS tone and the DCS code. Any of them can be wrong
Listen on the repeater's input frequency
A sub-audible tone sent with your voice to open the squelch
Two audio tones at the same time, like a phone keypad
What one repeater receives, every repeater in the network transmits
An ID that organizes traffic, so you only hear the group you want. Join by programming the group's ID
An access code programmed into your radio to reach a specific repeater
Configuration data loaded onto your radio for repeaters and talkgroups

pairs: A sub-audible tone that opens the squelch
Every repeater transmits what one receives
An ID that organizes DMR traffic
An access code for a specific DMR repeater
Configuration data loaded onto the radio
Can't get into a repeater you can hear
Offset, tone or code is wrong

compare.how: One tone, below what you can hear, sent with your voice.
Two audible tones at once, from the keypad. Used to send commands.
Which group of stations you hear. Pick it by entering its ID code.
Which repeater you can get into.
The file of settings that holds the repeaters and talkgroups.

traps.wrong: To listen on a repeater’s output frequency
traps.why: You can already hear the output. Reverse switches you to the input, so you hear the station talking into the repeater.
DTMF is the keypad's two audible tones. The sub-audible tone with your voice is CTCSS.
CTCSS is a single sub-audible tone. Two tones at once is DTMF.
A wrong offset is one reason, but so is a wrong CTCSS tone or DCS code. The answer is all of them.

traps.wrong: Program your radio with the DTMF tone used by the talkgroup
traps.why: Talkgroups use an ID or code programmed into the radio, not a DTMF tone.

traps.wrong: By enabling the group’s CTCSS tone
traps.why: On DMR you select a group by entering its identification code, not a CTCSS tone.

traps.wrong: A code which automatically programs the repeater offset to a frequency chosen by the user
traps.why: The color code doesn't set the offset. It's the access code for a specific repeater.

traps.wrong: An adapter cable used to connect a DMR radio to a computer for internet access
traps.why: A code plug isn't a cable or a plug. It's configuration data loaded onto the radio.
